title: Waveform Shapes
concept:
The shape of a waveform determines its timbre — the character or colour of a sound. Different waveform shapes contain different harmonic overtones on top of the fundamental frequency.

Sine wave: The purest sound. A single frequency, no overtones. Smooth and flute-like.

Square wave: Adds odd-numbered harmonics (3rd, 5th, 7th…). Produces a hollow, buzzy tone — think vintage video game sounds or a clarinet.

Sawtooth wave: Adds both odd and even harmonics in large amounts. Produces a bright, rich, brassy sound — great for leads and bass.

Triangle wave: Similar to sine but with a few odd harmonics. Sounds softer and rounder than square — somewhere between sine and square.

The Oscillator's Waveform control lets you switch between these shapes. Your task is to change it to Square and hear the difference.

task.instruction: Change the Oscillator's waveform to Square. Click the Waveform dropdown on the Oscillator component and select 'Square'. Listen to how the sound changes.
